title: Senior's toolkit: npm, Next.js and React DevTools
summary: Create, install, build and profile a React and Next.js app the way a team does, and read the errors you meet first.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: npm, Next.js and React DevTools
steps.body: On a React team most of the day is spent in a handful of commands and two browser tabs. These are the ones experienced front-end engineers use without looking them up.

toolkit.what: Create a Next.js app with TypeScript, a linter and the App Router set up (it asks for anything you do not pass as a flag). `@latest` makes sure you do not get an old cached generator.
Install exactly what `package-lock.json` says, from a clean `node_modules`. It never changes the lockfile, so CI and every teammate get the same versions.
flags: clean, exact, fails if package.json and the lockfile disagree
may update the lockfile; use it when you add or upgrade a package
toolkit.when: in CI, and after pulling a branch with dependency changes

toolkit.what: Run a script from package.json. `npm run` with no name lists them. Everything after `--` is passed on to the script's command.
flags: pass `-t cart` to the test runner
show which versions of a package are installed, and why

toolkit.what: The production build (`npm run build`). It type-checks the project and prints every route with how it is rendered: check it before you merge. (Run lint as its own script; Next.js 16 no longer lints during the build.)
flags: prerendered at build time for each value from `generateStaticParams`
rendered on the server for each request
Next.js 16 dropped the size and First Load JS columns; measure what a page ships with Lighthouse instead

toolkit.what: A browser extension. Select a component to see its props, state and hooks, and edit them live. Find the component that holds the wrong value.
flags: jump to the DOM element or the source
a setting that flashes every re-render

toolkit.what: Record an interaction and see which components rendered, how long each took, and why.
flags: a setting that names the props or state that changed
toolkit.example: F12 > Profiler > Record > type in search > Stop

toolkit.what: The two lint rules every React codebase turns on. They catch hooks called conditionally and effects that read stale values.
flags: hooks only at the top level of components and custom hooks
every value an effect reads is in its dependency array

steps.prompt: CI fails at the install step with this. What do you do?
code: npm error `npm ci` can only install packages when your package.json and package-lock.json
npm error are in sync. Please update your lock file with `npm install` before continuing.
options: Run `npm install` locally, check the lockfile diff, and commit `package-lock.json` with the package.json change
Change CI to run `npm install` instead of `npm ci`
steps.explain: Someone changed package.json without committing the updated lockfile. Switching CI to `npm install` or deleting the lockfile hides the problem and lets every build pick different versions.

steps.prompt: A search box shows results for the previous query, one keystroke behind. The effect is `useEffect(() => { load(query); }, []);` and lint shows a warning on that line. Which rule is it, and what is the fix?
options: `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps`: the effect reads `query`, so it must be `[query]`
There is no lint rule for this; add a `setTimeout`
steps.explain: With `[]` the effect runs once and keeps the first `query` it saw. Listing every value it reads makes it rerun when they change. (Add an `AbortController` cleanup too, so a slow old request cannot overwrite a newer one.)

After pulling main, to get exactly what the lockfile says
Adding a new package to the project

steps.prompt: Match each tool to the question it answers.
pairs: what props and state does this component have now?
why did the whole list re-render on each keystroke?
is this page static or rendered per request?
are two copies of React installed?
which scripts does this project have?

steps.prompt: You add the `zod` package on a branch. Put the steps in order, from your terminal to a green CI run.
lines: git commit -m "Validate checkout input with zod"

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: Use `npm ci` whenever you want what the lockfile says, and commit the lockfile with every dependency change. When a component is slow or shows the wrong value, open React DevTools before adding `console.log`, and read the `next build` route table before you merge.
